slides.title: Collaboration Quality Drives Outcomes
bullets: Determines both study success and how the company is seen locally
Not a one-off event but a relationship sustained over time
Needs clear rules protecting independence and ethical integrity

slides.title: Understand the Research Agenda First
bullets: What questions genuinely interest them, and at what career stage
What resources they have: time, team, funding, patient access
What kind of support could actually move their research forward
Built through longitudinal, genuine scientific exchange, not one talk

slides.title: The MSL as Process Facilitator
bullets: Explains the formal steps to submit a proposal, typically via IIS
Shares the review committee's criteria and realistic timelines
Clarifies what support the company can and cannot offer
States upfront that approval rests on independent scientific review

slides.title: Support Without Interference
bullets: Can facilitate access to relevant literature and product context data
Can connect investigators working on similar questions
Always through approved channels only
Never touches data analysis or results interpretation

slides.title: The Collaboration Doesn't End There
bullets: MSL can help results reach the right scientific audience
Congress presentations, non-promotional discussion, publication plans
Always respecting the investigator's authorship and intended message

slides.title: A Valued Partner, Not a Processor
bullets: Genuine scientific interest plus process transparency builds trust
Strict respect for ethical limits is non-negotiable
Together they make the MSL a long-term valued research partner

takeaway.title: Strong investigator collaboration is built on genuine interest, transparent process, and strict respect for scientific independence
bullets: Understanding the investigator's real agenda comes before any ask
MSL facilitates process and support but never the science itself
The relationship continues through publication, not just approval
